items.followUp: Differentiate between a solution and a suspension.

rubric.why: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout.
rubric.description: States that a homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its uniform composition.

rubric.why: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, often with distinguishable components or phases.
rubric.description: States that a heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition or distinguishable components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its non-uniform composition or distinguishable components.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout, and its components are not visibly distinguishable.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, and its components or phases can be distinguished.

items.followUp: How do positive and negative ions form?

rubric.description: Identifies a cation as a positively charged ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a cation is positive.

rubric.description: Identifies an anion as a negatively charged ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an anion is negative.

modelAnswer: A cation is a positively charged ion, usually formed when an atom loses one or more electrons.
An anion is a negatively charged ion, usually formed when an atom gains one or more electrons.

items.followUp: Write down two characteristics of protons.

rubric.why: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.description: States that a neutron is electrically neutral.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its zero charge.

rubric.why: A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is found in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Gives another characteristic of a neutron, such as its approximate mass or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its approximate mass of 1 amu or its location in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge; it is neutral.
A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu and is present in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: What is the difference between an energy level and an orbital?

rubric.why: A shell is a main energy level around the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies a shell as a main energy level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shells are main energy levels.

rubric.why: A subshell is a subdivision of a shell, commonly designated s, p, d or f.
rubric.description: Identifies subshells as divisions of shells or gives their designations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a subshell as a shell subdivision or naming its types.

modelAnswer: A shell is a main energy level of an atom and is represented by K, L, M, and so on.
A subshell is a subdivision of a shell and is represented by s, p, d, or f.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a period and a group in the periodic table.

rubric.why: Periods run horizontally across the periodic table; elements in a period have the same number of occupied shells.
rubric.description: Describes a period as a horizontal row or notes the shared number of shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either distinguishing feature of a period.

rubric.why: Groups run vertically; elements in a group have similar properties and typically the same number of valence electrons.
rubric.description: Describes a group as a vertical column or notes a characteristic shared by its elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either distinguishing feature of a group.

modelAnswer: A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table; its elements have the same number of occupied electron shells.
A group is a vertical column in the periodic table; its elements have similar chemical properties and usually the same number of valence electrons.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and give an example.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential definition.

rubric.why: The model example shows gaseous sodium losing an electron to form a sodium ion.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of ionization, such as sodium forming Na⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or equation.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom to form a positive ion.
For example: Na(g) + energy → Na⁺(g) + e⁻.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and give an example.

rubric.why: An ionic bond is an electrostatic attraction.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as a force of attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bond involves attraction.

rubric.why: The attraction is between oppositely charged ions produced by electron transfer.
rubric.description: Identifies the oppositely charged ions involved in an ionic bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying attraction between positive and negative ions.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
These ions are formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another.

items.followUp: What is a triple covalent bond? Give an example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond involves two shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: States that two pairs of electrons are shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two shared electron pairs.

rubric.why: Oxygen is a standard example of a molecule containing a double covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as O₂ or a C=O bond in CO₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two atoms share two pairs of electrons.
For example, the two oxygen atoms in an O₂ molecule are joined by a double covalent bond (O=O).
